title: The Clock of Vilna
premise: In the winter of 1919, in the contested city of Vilna, apprentice clockmaker August Dravenmoor is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock just as the bridge out of town closes for the season. Trapped among soldiers, refugees, and a city changing hands, she witnesses an atrocity that the advancing army intends to erase from history. Using her access to the clock tower and the observatory's records, August hides testimony inside the mechanism itself and copies it to sympathetic clerks, racing to get the truth on record before the armistice is signed and the victors' historians write their version. The book ends with the armistice signed and the official account falsified — but decades later, a restorer opening the clock finds August's hidden ledger, and the truth finally enters the record.
about_author: Emrys Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing displaced records from Eastern European observatories and municipal clocks. The Clock of Vilna grew out of a single marginal note found in a repair log dated 1919.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: August Dravenmoor, third-year apprentice in her uncle's workshop, receives an official summons to repair the observatory's master clock. Her POV establishes her belief that history happens elsewhere, to other people. Emotional beat: cautious pride masked by self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: August arrives in Vilna as military engineers announce the bridge will close for winter repairs. POV alternates between August and a wounded soldier, Tomas, waiting to cross. Beat: the trap springs quietly; August realizes she cannot leave.

chapters.title: Gears and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Inside the observatory, August meets the aging keeper, Professor Lelis, who guards more than instruments. Her POV. She begins the repair and senses the clock has been deliberately slowed. Beat: unease beneath professional fascination.

chapters.title: A City of Two Flags
chapters.summary: Vilna under joint occupation: Polish and German notices posted side by side. Tomas's POV as he convalesces in a converted schoolhouse. Beat: the ordinary cruelty of bureaucracy; August watches from the edges.

chapters.title: What the Clock Counts
chapters.summary: August discovers the escapement was tampered with to hide a gap in the observatory's time logs — someone erased hours. Her POV. Beat: first inkling that records here are weapons.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Kept Copies
chapters.summary: August befriends Miriam, a municipal clerk secretly duplicating deportation orders. Miriam's POV. Beat: hope kindled by quiet resistance; August learns paper can outlive armies.

chapters.title: Snow on the Observatory Steps
chapters.summary: First heavy snow; the city seals inward. August's POV as she works nights on the clock, listening to soldiers below plan something they don't name. Beat: dread accumulating like snowfall.

chapters.title: Tomas's Testimony
chapters.summary: Tomas tells August what he saw at a village outside Vilna before his unit was disbanded. His POV, fragmented. Beat: horror arriving secondhand but undeniable; August can no longer claim ignorance.

chapters.title: The Order
chapters.summary: August overhears officers ordering the observatory's archives seized and 'reconciled' with the official campaign history. Her POV. Beat: the enemy acquires a face — not violence, but erasure.

chapters.title: Lelis's Confession
chapters.summary: Professor Lelis admits he slowed the clock himself, to buy time for the archive, and asks August to finish what he started. His POV. Beat: passing of the torch; fear transmuted into duty.

chapters.title: Learning to Hide Hours
chapters.summary: August engineers hidden compartments in the clock's case using her craft. Her POV, technical and intimate. Beat: competence becoming courage; the clock becomes a vault.

chapters.title: Miriam's List
chapters.summary: Miriam shows August the duplicated orders naming hundreds deported from the Jewish quarter. Miriam's POV. Beat: grief and resolve; the abstract becomes names.

chapters.title: The Search
chapters.summary: Soldiers ransack the observatory looking for 'seditious documents.' August hides the first testimony pages inside the pendulum housing. Her POV. Beat: terror at close range; survival by stillness.

chapters.title: An Offer of Safety
chapters.summary: A Polish officer, Captain Wierzbicki, offers August passage out if she testifies only to what serves his faction. Her POV. Beat: temptation; justice revealed as negotiable currency.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: August declines, losing her only exit. Tomas's POV watching her choose. Beat: the price of integrity made concrete; loneliness deepens.

chapters.title: The Clock Stops
chapters.summary: Sabotage — or accident? — halts the master clock days before the armistice deadline. August's POV. Beat: crisis; the symbol of the story literally fails.

chapters.title: Repair Under Watch
chapters.summary: August repairs the clock while a garrison clerk observes her every move, forcing her to work blind on the hiding places. Her POV. Beat: tension through craftsmanship; performance of innocence.

chapters.title: Night Copyists
chapters.summary: Miriam, August, and two students copy testimonies by candlelight in the observatory basement. Rotating POVs. Beat: fragile community; laughter amid fear.

chapters.title: Betrayal Suspected
chapters.summary: One copyist goes missing; August suspects informers within the group. Her POV, paranoid and grieving. Beat: trust fractures; the cost of conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Missing Student
chapters.summary: The missing student is found detained, having confessed under duress. Tomas's POV as soldiers prepare to search again. Beat: countdown pressure; no safe place remains.

chapters.title: Splitting the Record
chapters.summary: August divides the testimony into three caches: the clock, the church crypt, and Miriam's office wall. Her POV. Beat: strategic clarity born of desperation.

chapters.title: Wierzbicki's Warning
chapters.summary: The captain privately warns August the armistice may fail and the city will change hands again — worse men are coming. His conflicted POV. Beat: ambiguous ally; the stakes widen.

chapters.title: The Deportation Train
chapters.summary: August witnesses a deportation train at the freight yard and memorizes numbers, faces, times. Her POV, restrained and devastating. Beat: witness as burden; invisibility finally impossible.

chapters.title: Writing It Down
chapters.summary: August writes her own testimony through the night, hands shaking. Her POV. Beat: transformation from mechanic to witness; memory committed to ink.

chapters.title: Lelis Collapses
chapters.summary: The professor suffers a stroke mid-sentence while dictating his final deposition. August's POV at his bedside. Beat: mortality pressing the deadline; inheritance of unfinished work.

chapters.title: The Armistice Rumor
chapters.summary: News spreads that terms are being drafted in Paris; whichever army holds the archives will shape the peace. Multiple brief POVs across the city. Beat: the race formalized; history as jurisdiction.

chapters.title: Seizure of the Archives
chapters.summary: Soldiers crate the observatory's official records for removal. August watches her cover stories tested. Her POV. Beat: near-catastrophe; one cache nearly discovered.

chapters.title: Miriam's Choice
chapters.summary: Miriam must decide whether to flee with her family or stay to guard the office cache until the armistice signs. Her POV. Beat: heartbreak; the theme of survival's price embodied.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Armistice eve. August keeps the clock running through the night as artillery echoes far off. Her POV, meditative. Beat: stillness before the storm; the clock as heartbeat of the city.

chapters.title: Signing Day
chapters.summary: The armistice is signed; the victors immediately begin writing the official history, omitting the deportations. August's POV reading the first gazette. Beat: bitter vindication deferred; fury at print.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: A final sweep targets 'unauthorized documents.' Soldiers tear open the clock case while August stands by. Her POV. Beat: climax threshold; everything hangs on one hidden seam.

chapters.title: The Seam Holds
chapters.summary: The searchers find nothing; the compartment's craftsmanship defeats them. August's POV, adrenaline draining into tears. Beat: relief and exhaustion; craft as salvation.

chapters.title: What Miriam Paid
chapters.summary: August learns Miriam stayed behind and was detained during the raid, protecting the office cache. Tomas's POV. Beat: grief and guilt; survival's cost made personal.

chapters.title: Testimony Before the Commission
chapters.summary: An Allied commission arrives collecting depositions. August testifies, knowing her words may vanish into the same files. Her POV. Beat: courage without guarantee; speaking anyway.

chapters.title: The Bridge Reopens
chapters.summary: Spring; the bridge reopens and August could leave. She chooses to stay until Lelis can be moved and the caches secured. Her POV. Beat: agency reclaimed; home chosen, not defaulted.

chapters.title: Handing Over the Keys
chapters.summary: August entrusts the clock's secret to a young restorer's apprentice, drawing him a diagram he doesn't yet understand. Her POV. Beat: transmission; memory entrusted to the future.

chapters.title: Departure
chapters.summary: August crosses the bridge at last, carrying a single copied page sewn into her coat. Her POV. Beat: bittersweet release; the city receding but never left behind.

chapters.title: Years Later
chapters.summary: Epilogue-shift: 1968, a clock restorer opens the Vilna observatory clock and finds August's hidden ledger, names intact. His POV. Beat: quiet triumph; the record survives its keepers.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: The ledger is authenticated and read aloud at a memorial; the erased names enter the public record. Restorer's POV closing into August's final line from her old age. Beat: justice outside the law, achieved by patience and craft.

chapters.title: The Clock Still Runs
chapters.summary: Final chapter returns to the present of 1919's aftermath: August, old, visits the repaired clock, hearing it keep true time. Her POV. Beat: reconciliation with memory; the price paid acknowledged as worth it.
